tests.title: cli.SiblingCommands is an untyped constant with the exact sibling sentence
given: the internal/cli package
tests.when: the constant is compared with the expected text and concatenated with a raw-string constant in a const declaration
then: cli.SiblingCommands equals "spec writes a package from an idea, specr renders one, speca reports and changes its state."
the const expression `const x = "a\n" + cli.SiblingCommands` compiles
tests.pseudocode: const probe = "a\n" + cli.SiblingCommands; assert cli.SiblingCommands == "spec writes a package from an idea, specr renders one, speca reports and changes its state."; assert probe != ""

tests.title: The sibling sentence is written in exactly one non-test Go file
given: the repository tree
tests.when: every non-test .go file under the repository is scanned for the sibling sentence text
then: exactly one file contains it
that file is under internal/cli
no file under cmd/spec, cmd/specr or cmd/speca contains it
tests.pseudocode: hits = [f for f in walk('**/*.go') if not f.endswith('_test.go') and SENTENCE in read(f)]; assert len(hits)==1; assert hits[0].startswith('internal/cli/')

tests.title: -h and --help of each command print the sibling line between title and Usage
given: the spec, specr and speca entry points run in process with captured stdout and stderr
tests.when: each command is invoked with -h and then with --help
then: the exit code is 0
stdout is empty

stderr contains "

" + cli.SiblingCommands + "

" before the first "Usage:"
the title line precedes the sibling line
tests.pseudocode:
for cmd in [spec, specr, speca]: for flag in ['-h','--help']: code,out,err = cmd.Main([flag]); assert code==0; assert out==''; i=err.index('Usage:'); assert ('

'+SiblingCommands+'

') in err[:i]

tests.title: A bare invocation of each command exits 2 with a usage envelope and the sibling line on stderr
given: stdout is not a terminal
the spec, specr and speca entry points run in process
tests.when: each command is invoked with no arguments
then: the exit code is 2
stdout holds an envelope with error category usage
stderr contains cli.SiblingCommands
tests.pseudocode: for cmd in [spec, specr, speca]: code,out,err = cmd.Main([]); assert code==2; assert decode(out).error.category=='usage'; assert SiblingCommands in err

tests.title: specr help describes next as naming the render target and the speca claim or done call
given: specr is run with --help
tests.when: the help text on stderr is read
then: the paragraph describing next mentions "speca" and the claim or done call
the help still contains "specr <spec> --task N"
the exit code is 0 and stdout is empty
tests.pseudocode: code,out,err = specr.Main(['--help']); para = paragraph_containing(err,'next'); assert 'speca' in para; assert 'specr <spec> --task N' in err

tests.title: speca help carries the constant and not the old wording
given: speca is run with --help
tests.when: the help text on stderr is read
then: it contains cli.SiblingCommands
it does not contain "speca reports its state"
tests.pseudocode: code,out,err = speca.Main(['--help']); assert SiblingCommands in err; assert 'speca reports its state' not in err

tests.title: Each command's package doc names the other two commands in one sentence
given: the cmd/spec, cmd/specr and cmd/speca packages parsed with go/parser
tests.when: each package doc comment is split into sentences
then: for each command some single sentence contains the names of both other commands
tests.pseudocode: for pkg,others in {spec:[specr,speca], specr:[spec,speca], speca:[spec,specr]}: doc = parse_pkg_doc('cmd/'+pkg); assert any(all(o in s for o in others) for s in sentences(doc))

tests.title: specr --schema description is its own sentence plus one space plus the sibling sentence
given: specr is run with --schema
tests.when: the JSON document on stdout is decoded
then: the exit code is 0
description starts with the pre-existing specr sentence
description ends with " " + cli.SiblingCommands
tests.pseudocode: code,out,_ = specr.Main(['--schema']); d = json(out).description; assert code==0; assert d.startswith(specrSentence+' '); assert d.endswith(' '+SiblingCommands)

tests.title: speca --schema description ends with the sibling sentence and holds no other copy
given: speca is run with --schema
tests.when: the JSON document on stdout is decoded
then: the exit code is 0
description ends with " " + cli.SiblingCommands
the sibling sentence occurs exactly once in the description
the old wording "speca reports its state" is absent
tests.pseudocode: code,out,_ = speca.Main(['--schema']); d = json(out).description; assert code==0; assert d.endswith(' '+SiblingCommands); assert d.count(SiblingCommands)==1; assert 'reports its state' not in d

tests.title: Both schema golden files match and differ from the previous ones only in description
given: the checked-in cmd/specr/testdata/schema.golden.json and cmd/speca/testdata/schema.golden.json
UPDATE_GOLDEN is not set
tests.when: TestSchemaGolden runs for specr and speca and the golden documents are decoded
then: both goldens match the live --schema output byte for byte
the flags, result and exit_codes members are unchanged: no flag or result field added or removed
each golden description ends with the sibling sentence
tests.pseudocode: for cmd in [specr, speca]: live = cmd.schema(); assert bytes(live)==read(golden); g=json(live); assert g.description.endswith(SiblingCommands); assert 'writable' not in str(g.result)

tests.title: IntentDrift is true only for an active package whose intent hash is set and fails or differs
given: specs built in memory with a PRD body that has an ## Intent section
tests.when: IntentDrift is called for each status with a matching hash, a different hash, an unset hash, and a body without ## Intent
then: active + set + matching hash gives false
active + set + different hash gives true
active + set + body without ## Intent (hash error) gives true
active + unset hash gives false
draft, sealed, superseded and archived give false even with a different hash
tests.pseudocode: h,_ = ComputeIntentHash(body); assert !IntentDrift(spec(active,&h,body)); assert IntentDrift(spec(active,&"x",body)); assert IntentDrift(spec(active,&h,'no intent')); assert !IntentDrift(spec(active,nil,body)); for s in [draft,sealed,superseded,archived]: assert !IntentDrift(spec(s,&"x",body))

tests.title: Writable equals (draft) or (active and no intent drift) for every combination
given: a generator over statuses {draft, active, sealed, superseded, archived}, IntentHash set or unset, and PRD bodies that match, mismatch or lack ## Intent
tests.when: for any generated spec, Writable is called
then: the result equals status==draft || (status==active && !IntentDrift(spec))
tests.pseudocode: for spec in gen_specs(): assert Writable(spec) == (spec.Status=='draft' or (spec.Status=='active' and not IntentDrift(spec)))

tests.title: IntentDrift and Writable return false for a nil spec without panicking
given: a nil *afspec.Spec
tests.when: IntentDrift(nil) and Writable(nil) are called
then: both return false
neither panics
tests.pseudocode: assert IntentDrift(nil)==false; assert Writable(nil)==false

tests.title: speca decides drift and writability only through specpkg and its envelopes are unchanged
given: temp repositories holding a draft package, an active package without drift, an active package with drift, and a sealed package
no non-test Go function in cmd/speca computes intent drift
tests.when: speca report, list and a task form are run on each package and the cmd/speca sources are scanned for afspec.ComputeIntentHash
then: the report intent_drift is true only for the drifted package
the task form on the drifted and sealed packages is refused at stage status
the claim suggestion appears only for writable packages
no non-test file in cmd/speca calls ComputeIntentHash or declares intentDrift
tests.pseudocode: for p in pkgs: r=speca(p); assert r.intent_drift == IntentDrift(load(p)); assert refused(speca(p,'--task','1','--state','in_progress')) == !Writable(load(p)); assert 'ComputeIntentHash' not in cmd_speca_sources

tests.title: specr keeps writability in an unexported field that never reaches the JSON or schema
given: specr run on a draft package and on a sealed package
tests.when: the Result is built, marshalled and the --schema document is produced
then: the Result's unexported writable field equals specpkg.Writable of the loaded package
the JSON result has no key containing writable or intent_drift
the --schema result description has no such key
tests.pseudocode: res = execute(draftRef); assert res.writable==true; res2 = execute(sealedRef); assert res2.writable==false; assert 'writable' not in json(res) and 'intent_drift' not in json(res); assert 'writable' not in schema_json

tests.title: A whole render of a writable idle package offers the claim of the first task, then the render suggestion
given: a draft package with three pending tasks, task 1 has no depends_on, no task in progress
tests.when: specr <spec> is run without --task
then: next has exactly two elements
next[0] is tool speca, input equal to result.spec_dir, flags [--task, 1, --state, in_progress]
next[0].why contains the task id, its title and the word claim
next[1] is tool specr with flags [--task, 1]
next[0].input equals next[1].input and len(next[0].flags) == 4
tests.pseudocode: r = specr(repo,'09_agent_mode'); n=r.next; assert len(n)==2; assert n[0]=={tool:'speca',input:r.result.spec_dir,flags:['--task','1','--state','in_progress']}; assert 'claim' in n[0].why and title1 in n[0].why; assert n[1].tool=='specr' and n[1].flags==['--task','1']

tests.title: A whole render with --section or --max-tokens still offers the claim and names the first unfinished ready task
given: a draft package where task 1 is done and task 2 is pending with depends_on [1]
tests.when: specr is run with --section tasks, and again with --max-tokens set
then: next[0] is the claim of task 2
next[1] is specr --task 2
tests.pseudocode: mark_done(1); for extra in [['--section','tasks'],['--max-tokens','2000']]: n=specr(spec,*extra).next; assert n[0].flags==['--task','2','--state','in_progress']; assert n[1].flags==['--task','2']

tests.title: A whole render with any task in progress offers no speca entry
given: a draft package where task 2 is in_progress and task 1 is pending and ready
tests.when: specr <spec> is run without --task
then: next holds no element with tool speca
next holds the unchanged render suggestion --task 1
tests.pseudocode: set_state(2,'in_progress'); n=specr(spec).next; assert all(e.tool!='speca' for e in n); assert n==[render_suggestion(1)]

tests.title: A whole render whose first unfinished task is not ready offers no speca entry
given: a draft package where task 1 is pending with depends_on [2] and task 2 is pending
tests.when: specr <spec> is run without --task
then: next holds no element with tool speca
next holds the render suggestion naming task 1
tests.pseudocode: set_depends_on(1,[2]); n=specr(spec).next; assert all(e.tool!='speca' for e in n); assert n[0].tool=='specr' and n[0].flags==['--task','1']

tests.title: A whole render of a package that cannot take a write offers no speca entry
given: otherwise idle packages with status sealed, superseded, archived, and an active one whose PRD intent no longer matches the recorded IntentHash
tests.when: specr <spec> is run on each without --task
then: for every package next holds no element with tool speca
the render suggestion for task 1 is still present
tests.pseudocode: for p in [sealed,superseded,archived,active_drift]: n=specr(p).next; assert all(e.tool!='speca' for e in n); assert n[0].tool=='specr'

tests.title: A whole render with every task done or dropped produces no next entries
given: a draft package whose tasks are all done or dropped
tests.when: specr <spec> is run without --task
then: the exit code is 0
next is empty or absent in the envelope
tests.pseudocode: set_all(['done','dropped','done']); r=specr(spec); assert r.exit==0; assert len(r.next or [])==0

tests.title: specr's whole-render claim equals speca's report claim for any package state
given: a generator of package states: status, intent hash set or unset and matching or not, task states, and depends_on lists including absent and explicit []
tests.when: for any generated package, specr <spec> and speca <spec> are both run
then: the claim entries (tool speca, flags ending --state in_progress) of both envelopes are equal element by element, or both absent
when present, the claimed task equals the task named by specr's render suggestion
tests.pseudocode: for pkg in gen_pkgs(): a=claims(specr(pkg).next); b=claims(speca(pkg).next); assert a==b; if a: assert a[0].flags[1]==render_sugg(specr(pkg).next).flags[1]

tests.title: A task render of a pending ready task offers its claim first, even with another task in progress
given: a draft package where task 1 is pending with no depends_on, task 3 is in_progress
tests.when: specr <spec> --task 1 is run
then: next[0] is tool speca with flags [--task, 1, --state, in_progress] and a why saying to claim task 1 before working on it
next[1] is the specr render suggestion for the next unfinished task after 1
tests.pseudocode: set_state(3,'in_progress'); n=specr(spec,'--task','1').next; assert n[0].tool=='speca' and n[0].flags==['--task','1','--state','in_progress']; assert 'claim' in n[0].why; assert n[1].tool=='specr'

tests.title: A task render of an in-progress task offers the done call first
given: a draft package where task 1 is in_progress
tests.when: specr <spec> --task 1 is run
then: next[0] is tool speca with flags [--task, 1, --state, done] and a why saying to record task 1 done once its work is finished and its tests pass
next[1] is specr --task 2
tests.pseudocode: set_state(1,'in_progress'); n=specr(spec,'--task','1').next; assert n[0]=={tool:'speca',input:dir,flags:['--task','1','--state','done'],why:ANY}; assert 'done' in n[0].why; assert n[1].flags==['--task','2']

tests.title: A task render of a pending task that is not ready offers no speca entry
given: a draft package where task 2 is pending with depends_on [1] and task 1 is pending
tests.when: specr <spec> --task 2 is run
then: next holds no element with tool speca
next holds the render suggestion --task 3
tests.pseudocode: n=specr(spec,'--task','2').next; assert all(e.tool!='speca' for e in n); assert n==[render_suggestion(3)]

tests.title: A task render of a done or dropped task offers no speca entry
given: a draft package where task 1 is done and task 2 is dropped
tests.when: specr <spec> --task 1 and specr <spec> --task 2 are run
then: neither next holds an element with tool speca
tests.pseudocode: for t in [1,2]: n=specr(spec,'--task',str(t)).next; assert all(e.tool!='speca' for e in n)

tests.title: A task render of a non-writable package offers no speca entry for any task state
given: sealed, superseded, archived and drifted-active packages, each with a pending ready task 1 and, in a variant, task 1 in_progress
tests.when: specr <spec> --task 1 is run on each package and variant
then: no next holds an element with tool speca
tests.pseudocode: for p in non_writable: for st in ['pending','in_progress']: set_state(p,1,st); assert all(e.tool!='speca' for e in specr(p,'--task','1').next)

tests.title: The specr render suggestion is unchanged in rule, flags and why
given: a draft package in whole-render, task-render and all-done states
tests.when: the specr element of next is compared with the pre-change rule: first task after N (or first overall) not done or dropped
then: its flags are [--task, id]
its why is "task %d (%s) is the first task not done; render the package scoped to it" after a whole render and "task %d (%s) is the next task not done" after a task render
when no unfinished task remains the specr element is absent and next holds only the speca entry or nothing
tests.pseudocode: n=specr(spec).next; s=[e for e in n if e.tool=='specr'][0]; assert s.why==fmt('task %d (%s) is the first task not done; render the package scoped to it',1,t1); n=specr(spec,'--task','3').next; assert [e for e in n if e.tool=='specr']==[]

tests.title: A --markdown-file write failure still emits next with the same entries
given: a draft package with task 1 pending and ready
--markdown-file names a path in a directory that does not exist
tests.when: specr <spec> --markdown-file <bad path> is run, and again without --markdown-file
then: the first exits 1 with result and next present
its next equals the next of the successful render
tests.pseudocode: bad=specr(spec,'--markdown-file','/nonexistent/x.md'); ok=specr(spec); assert bad.exit==1; assert bad.next==ok.next and bad.next[0].tool=='speca'

tests.title: A package that cannot be loaded produces an error and no next
given: a spec reference that resolves to no package or to a package with malformed JSON
tests.when: specr is run on it
then: the exit code is 1
the envelope has an error
the envelope has no next
tests.pseudocode: r=specr('99_missing'); assert r.exit==1; assert r.error!=None; assert r.next in (None,[])

tests.title: specr leaves every package file byte-identical, including when next holds a speca entry
given: a draft package with a pending ready task 1 and an in-progress variant
a hash of every file in the package directory
tests.when: specr is run whole, with --task 1 in each variant
then: every file hash is identical before and after each call
no file is created or removed in the package
tests.pseudocode: before=hash_dir(pkg); specr(spec); specr(spec,'--task','1'); assert hash_dir(pkg)==before

tests.title: An agent renders a package, runs the suggested claim through speca and tasks.json records task 1 in progress
given: a temp repository with a draft package, three pending tasks, none in progress
tests.when: specr <spec> is run, then the first next entry is run as a speca call
then: specr's next[0] is the claim of task 1
speca exits 0 and tasks.json on disk shows task 1 in_progress
specr's own call changed nothing on disk before the claim
tests.pseudocode: r=specr(spec); c=r.next[0]; assert c.tool=='speca'; out=speca(c.input,*c.flags); assert out.exit==0; assert load(tasks).task(1).state=='in_progress'

tests.title: An agent renders its in-progress task and records it done through speca
given: a temp repository with a writable package where task 1 is in_progress
tests.when: specr <spec> --task 1 is run, then next[0] is run as a speca call
then: next[0] is the done call of task 1 and next[1] is specr --task 2
speca exits 0 and tasks.json on disk shows task 1 done
tests.pseudocode: set_state(1,'in_progress'); r=specr(spec,'--task','1'); c=r.next[0]; assert c.flags==['--task','1','--state','done']; assert speca(c.input,*c.flags).exit==0; assert load(tasks).task(1).state=='done'

tests.title: A reader of any command's help or schema learns of the other two
given: the spec, specr and speca commands built from the repository
tests.when: spec --help, specr --help, speca --help, specr --schema and speca --schema are run
then: each exits 0
each help on stderr carries the sibling line before Usage:
each schema document on stdout has a description ending with the sibling sentence
tests.pseudocode: for c in [spec,specr,speca]: assert c.Main(['--help']).exit==0 and SiblingCommands in stderr; for c in [specr,speca]: assert json(c.Main(['--schema']).stdout).description.endswith(SiblingCommands)
